summary: Whatever is heard: the voice of a man, a woman or a beast, by which one is known (“the voice is the voice of Jacob”), and the sound of things, a horn, feet, wings, many waters, rain, millstones, war in the camp. Yahweh's voice is heard in the thunder, whose plural קֹלוֹת is the word for thunder, and at Sinai Israel heard “the voice of words” and saw no form. To “hear the voice” of someone, שָׁמַע בְּקוֹל, is to do what he says, the obedience of Abraham and the covenant's condition; and a voice made to pass through the land is a proclamation. The Aramaic קָל of Daniel and the Peshitta's קָלָא are the same word, and Ugaritic ql, Phoenician ql and Ge'ez qāl “voice”, with Arabic qawl “saying”, show it is old and common to the Semitic languages.

words.gloss: voice; sound, noise; thunder; proclamation; hark!
words.summary: About five hundred times, in every part of scripture. Its spelling varies between קוֹל and קֹל; plural קֹלוֹת. It is what the ear takes in, set beside אִמְרָה “word” (Gen 4:23; Isa 28:23) and contrasted with תְּמוּנָה “form” (Deu 4:12), so the sense always turns on hearing, and a “voice” can be a cry, a word, a command or a report.

senses.definition: The voice by which a man or woman is known and heard, raised to call, cry or weep; and the cry of beasts and birds.

evidence.note: “הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב, but the hands are the hands of Esau”: the voice that tells who is speaking.
“Is this your voice (הֲקֹלְךָ), my son David?” and Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
Hagar “lifted her voice and wept”.
“I raised my voice and called out.”
“Let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet.”
Young lions roared, “they gave their voice”.
The birds “give voice” from among the branches.
“The voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.”
Jer 31:15, “a voice (קוֹל) is heard in Ramah”, fulfilled at Bethlehem; the Peshitta keeps קָלָא.

senses.definition: The voice of one who prays: what Yahweh is asked to hear, set beside “my supplications”.

evidence.note: “Lord, hear my voice (בְקוֹלִי); let your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications.”
“Hear the voice of my pleas when I cry to you.”
“I love him because Yahweh hears my voice, my pleas.”
“With my voice I call to Yahweh, and he answers me from his holy mountain.”

senses.definition: The sound of something heard and not seen: footsteps, a horn, wings, many waters, a coming shower, marching, millstones, thorns crackling, the noise of a camp at war or at a feast.

evidence.note: Joshua hears “the noise of the people” and says “a noise of war in the camp”.
Moses tells the sounds apart: not the sound of strength nor of weakness, but “the sound of singing I hear”.
Ahijah, blind, hears “the sound of her feet” at the door.
They heard “the sound of Yahweh God walking in the garden”.
“The sound of a shofar, very strong.”
“When you hear the sound of the shofar.”
The sound of the wings of the living creatures, “like the sound of many waters … the sound of a camp”.
“The sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees.”
“The sound of the roar of rain.”
“Like the sound of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool.”
“The sound of joy … of the bridegroom and of the bride, the sound of the millstones”, all to cease.
Jer 25:10 applied to Babylon the great: “the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard in you no more”.
“If the trumpet gives an uncertain sound (Peshitta קָלָא)”: the shofar's signal for war.

senses.gloss: thunder; Yahweh's voice in the storm
senses.definition: Thunder: the plural קֹלוֹת “voices” with hail or rain, and “the voice of Yahweh” in the storm, by which he speaks his power over the waters and the land.

evidence.note: “Yahweh gave קֹלֹת and hail, and fire ran down to the earth.”
“The קֹלוֹת will cease and there will be no more hail, that you may know the earth is Yahweh's.”
“I will call to Yahweh and he will give קֹלוֹת and rain”, in the wheat harvest.
“The voice of Yahweh is over the waters; the God of glory thunders (הִרְעִים).”
“The voice of Yahweh breaks the cedars.”
“The voice of your thunder (קוֹל רַעַמְךָ) was in the whirlwind.”
At creation the waters fled “from the voice of your thunder”.
“He thunders with the voice of his majesty.”
“A way for the lightning of the קֹלוֹת.”
“Yahweh thundered with a great voice against the Philistines.”
“Yahweh thundered in the heavens, and the Most High gave his voice.”
“Thunders and voices and lightnings and an earthquake”: the Sinai storm of Exo 19:16.
The voice from heaven: the crowd “said it had thundered”.

senses.definition: Yahweh's voice speaking words to men: at Sinai out of the fire, to Moses from above the ark, to Elijah and the prophets, and from heaven to Jesus. Israel heard a voice and saw no form.

evidence.note: “You heard קוֹל דְּבָרִים, the sound of words, and saw no form; only a voice.”
“Did a people ever hear the voice of God speaking out of the fire, as you have heard, and live?”
“From heaven he made you hear his voice, to instruct you.”
The ten words spoken “with a great voice, and he added no more”.
“Moses spoke, and God answered him בְקוֹל, with a voice.”
Moses “heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat”.
Not in wind, earthquake or fire, but “a voice of thin stillness”.
“And behold, a voice came to him and said, What are you doing here, Elijah?”
“I heard the voice of the Lord saying, Whom shall I send?”
At Horeb Israel asked not to hear the voice of Yahweh again; Yahweh answered with the promise of a prophet like Moses (Deu 18:15, 18).
“A voice (Peshitta קָלָא) from the heavens, saying, This is my beloved Son.”
“A voice from the cloud … This is my beloved Son …; hear him.”
“This voice we heard brought from heaven, when we were with him on the holy mountain.”
Sinai: “the sound of a trumpet and the voice of words”, Deu 4:12.
“Whose voice then shook the earth.”

senses.definition: With שָׁמַע and בְּ or לְ, to hear someone's voice is to do what he says: Adam with his wife, Abraham with Sarai and with God, a son with his parents, Israel with Yahweh. Not to hear his voice is disobedience.

evidence.note: “Because you listened to the voice of your wife and ate of the tree which I commanded you not to eat.”
“Because Abraham listened to my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes and my laws.”
The seed promise sworn after the offering of Isaac, “because you listened to my voice”.
“Abram listened to the voice of Sarai.”
A stubborn and rebellious son “who does not listen to the voice of his father or the voice of his mother”.
“If you will indeed listen to my voice and keep my covenant.”
Blessing “if you listen to the voice of Yahweh your God, to keep and do all his commandments”.
“Has Yahweh delight in burnt offerings as in listening to the voice of Yahweh? To listen is better than sacrifice.”
“Listen to my voice, and I will be your God and you shall be my people.”
“Today, if you will listen to his voice.”
Psa 95:7 quoted: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts”.
“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.”

senses.definition: A word sent out to be heard by many: with הֶעֱבִיר “make a voice pass through” the camp or the kingdom, a proclamation; or news that is heard, a report.

evidence.note: “Moses commanded, and they made a voice pass through the camp, saying, Let no man or woman make any more work.”
Cyrus “made a voice pass through all his kingdom, and also in writing”.
A voice made to pass through the cities: go out and bring branches for booths.
A voice made to pass through Israel from Beersheba to Dan for the passover.
“The report (הַקֹּל) was heard in Pharaoh's house: Joseph's brothers have come.”
“The sound of a report (קוֹל שְׁמוּעָה)! Behold, it comes, a great commotion from the land of the north.”

senses.definition: Standing alone at the head of a clause, “a voice!”, calling attention to what is heard before it is explained.

evidence.note: “קוֹל קוֹרֵא: in the wilderness prepare the way of Yahweh.”
“A voice says, Cry!”
“The voice of your watchmen! They lift up a voice, they sing together.”
“קוֹל דּוֹדִי! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains.”
“קוֹל דּוֹדִי דוֹפֵק: my beloved is knocking.”
“קוֹל דְּמֵי אָחִיךָ: your brother's blood is crying to me from the ground.”
Isa 40:3 of John the Baptist: “the voice of one crying in the wilderness”.
John: “I am the voice (Peshitta קָלָא) of one crying in the wilderness.”

evidence.locator: Isa.40.3, קוֹל → φωνή; Psa.95.7, בְּקֹלוֹ → φωνῆς; Jer.25.10; Jer.31.15; Deu.4.12; φωνή renders קוֹל ×434

evidence.note: Isa 40:3: “φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ”.
Psa 95:7: “if you hear his voice (τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ)”.
“His voice as the sound of many waters”: Ezk 1:24; 43:2.
Jer 25:10: “φωνὴ νυμφίου καὶ νύμφης”.

parallels.note: “Word, saying”: hear my voice, give ear to my word.

opposites.note: “Form, likeness”: at Horeb Israel heard a voice and saw no form.

phrases.gloss: lift up the voice (to weep, cry or sing)
raise the voice: call out, proclaim aloud
make a voice pass through: proclaim
the voice of bridegroom and bride: the life of a city in peace

words.summary: Seven times in Daniel: the Hebrew word in its Aramaic form.

senses.definition: The sound of the horn, pipe and other instruments at which all were to bow to the golden image; and the sound of the little horn's great words.

evidence.note: “When you hear the sound of the horn, pipe, lyre … fall down and worship the image of gold.”
“Because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking”, until the beast was slain.

senses.definition: A voice speaking: from heaven to Nebuchadnezzar, and the king's own anguished cry at the lions' den.

evidence.note: “While the word was in the king's mouth, a voice fell from heaven: … the kingdom has departed from you.”
Darius “cried with an anguished voice to Daniel”.

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܩܠܐ (qālā), its word for φωνή throughout the New Testament, used where it quotes the Hebrew קוֹל (Mat 3:3; Mat 2:18; Heb 3:7).

senses.definition: God's voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism, on the mountain and before his death, naming him his Son.

evidence.note: “וְהָא קָלָא מֵן שְׁמַיָּא: This is my beloved Son.”
“Father, glorify your name.” A voice was heard from heaven.
“This voice did not come for my sake but for yours.”

senses.gloss: voice heard and followed; the voice that raises the dead
senses.definition: The shepherd's voice his sheep hear and follow, the voice to be heard “today”, and the voice of the Son of God that the dead in the graves will hear.

evidence.note: “The sheep hear his voice (קָלֵה), and he calls his own sheep by name.”
Psa 95:7: “today, if you hear his voice (בְּקָלֵה)”.
“All who are in the graves will hear his voice (קָלֵה).”

senses.definition: The sound of an instrument, a trumpet, many waters.

evidence.note: Pipe or harp that “give a sound (יָהבָּן קָלָא)”.
“His voice like the sound of many waters.”

cognates.note: The same noun, with the same long ō; Ugaritic too says a voice is “given”, as Hebrew נָתַן קוֹל.

evidence.locator: pp. 173–174, *qwl: Ug. ql “voice, sound” with Ethiopic qāl
SEM000342 qwl [voice] N, UGC003465 ql [voice] N

cognates.note: Above all in the closing formula of votive inscriptions, “he heard his voice; may he bless him”: the voice of one praying that a god hears, as Psa 116:1 and 130:2.

evidence.locator: pp. 425–426, QL: KAI 41.6 šmʿ ql ybrk “he heard his voice; may he bless him”; KAI 63.3 šmʿ ql dbry “he heard the sound of his words”
SEM000342 qwl [voice] N, PUN001792 ql [voice] N

cognates.note: Ge'ez and Amharic carry it from “voice” to “word, saying”, as Arabic does.

evidence.locator: pp. 173–174, *qwl: Gz. n. qāl “voice, speech, sound” (Amharic rather “word”)
SEM000342 qwl [voice] N, GEZ004256 qāl [voice] N
Amharic ቃል (ḳal), noun: word, voice, sound, speech; etymology names Ge'ez ቃል (ḳal) and Hebrew קוֹל

cognates.note: Arabic has made the root its common verb “say”: the voice as what is uttered in words. The Hebrew keeps the sound, but its “voice” is often the words said: to hear the voice is to do what was said (Gen 3:17), and a voice is made to pass through the land as a proclamation (Exo 36:6).

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2994, art. قول, قَالَ (n42874)
evidence.note: “He said”; its object “must be a complete proposition … or a word signifying a command or the like; or a word significant of a sound.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2995, art. قول, قَوْلٌ (n42877)
evidence.note: “A saying; something said: and speech, or diction.”

cognates.gloss: voice, sound; rumour; (בַּת קָל) a voice from heaven
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the same word as Daniel's קָל, and the Targums use it for Hebrew קוֹל (Gen 27:22; Ezk 11:13); plural קָלַיָּא for the thunders of Exo 9:23, 29.

evidence.locator: s.v. קַל III (קָל, קָלָא), citing Targ. Gen. XXVII, 22; Targ. Ez. XI, 13; Targ. Ex. IX, 23, 29 (pl. קָלַיָּא); B. Bath. 5a רמא ביה ק׳ “raised his voice against him”

cognates.note: The chief as the one whose word commands, as Arabic qāla “say”: named, as possible only, on the sense “proclamation”, the voice that carries a command. Argued, not shown.

evidence.locator: p. 449, QWL, n. qwl, pl. ʾqwl “tribal leader, chief”, comparing the root's sense “speak” > “command”

doctrine.statement: Jesus says that “all who are in the graves will hear his voice and come out”, those who did good to a resurrection of life and those who did evil to a resurrection of judgment, and that those who hear will live (Jhn 5:25, 28–29); Paul says the Lord himself will come down from heaven “with the voice of an archangel and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will rise” (1Th 4:16). The dead are in the graves, sleeping in the dust (Dan 12:2), until a voice calls them out; they do not hear it until Christ comes. Life is given then, at the resurrection, not at death.

To hear Yahweh's voice is to do what he says. The promise to Abraham's seed was confirmed “because you listened to my voice” (Gen 22:18; 26:5); Israel's covenant rested on “if you will indeed listen to my voice” (Exo 19:5); and Samuel told Saul that listening to the voice of Yahweh is better than sacrifice (1Sa 15:22). The letter to the Hebrews takes Psa 95:7, “today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts”, as spoken to believers now (Heb 3:7–8, 15), and Jesus' sheep are those who hear his voice and follow him (Jhn 10:27). Hearing that does not obey is not hearing in scripture's sense.

At Horeb Israel asked not to hear the voice of Yahweh again, and Yahweh promised instead a prophet like Moses from among their brothers: “to him you shall listen” (Deu 18:15–18). At Jesus' baptism and on the mountain a voice from heaven said “This is my beloved Son” and “hear him” (Mat 3:17; 17:5); Peter says the voice came from “God the Father” to Jesus (2Pe 1:17–18), and Acts names Jesus as the prophet Moses foretold (Act 3:22). The one who speaks is the one God; the one spoken of is his Son, the prophet raised up from among Israel, whom God commands men to hear.

When Yahweh spoke at Horeb, Israel “heard the sound of words, but saw no form; only a voice” (Deu 4:12), and Moses draws the consequence: because you saw no form, make no carved image in the likeness of anything (Deu 4:15–16). God made himself known by what he said, and is to be known so still.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key קול; no existing entry used it. qalal.json leaves קוֹל out and asks for this entry (see its note). Keys: s.au.ab (קוֹל, 506 tokens) is claimed; s.br.ac lists the same 506 surfaces under קלל and is left unclaimed, as BDB lists the same occurrences under two keys and only one is named. xs.ac.ab is Daniel's Aramaic קָל (7 tokens: Dan 3:5, 7, 10, 15; 4:28; 6:21; 7:11); xs.af.af and s.bm.an are zero-token cross-references (“see קול”) and are not claimed. The name קוֹלָיָה (s.au.ac) is in names/kolaiah.json. קֹל “lightness” (Jer 3:9) stays in qalal.json. Ugaritic page: Segert's glossary entry falls before the “200 Glossary” running head, so p. 199. Fisher's *qwl entry sits just before an OCR page number “174”; whether that number heads or foots the page is not clear from the OCR, so the locator gives pp. 173–174: check the scan. Krahmalkov's QL runs across the page break 425/426. Akkadian is left out: Oracc's qâlu “pay attention, be silent” and qūlu “silence” look like the consonants but mean the opposite; some compare an Akkadian qâlu “cry out”, not checked in CAD. Sabaic qwl “chief” is recorded as possible only and named only on the sense “proclamation”. Arabic قيل (qāla “nap at noon; cancel”) shares no sense and is not recorded. The Greek κηρύσσω renders הֶעֱבִיר קוֹל twice (Exo 36:6; 2Ch 36:22) and is not recorded. Open questions: (1) whether s.br.ac should also be claimed here so the word sheet shows this entry on every קוֹל token; (2) the Sabaic link, and whether Arabic qawl “saying” should stay a full cognate or be marked possible for the voice senses.
